title: Narrative Reward
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalography (EEG) recordings from 40 participants engaged in an interactive narrative task involving decision-making and feedback processing. Participants read a story with hierarchically-blocked narrative contexts, making yes/no decisions about items and receiving correctness feedback. The study contrasts narrative-rich conditions, where contextual information was provided at location transitions and sub-locations, with non-narrative conditions lacking such context. The experimental design explores how narrative framing influences neural responses to decision-making and reward feedback.
methods_description: EEG data were collected while participants performed an interactive narrative task. Participants made yes/no decisions about items presented with or without narrative context, and received feedback indicating decision correctness. Narrative trials were hierarchically organized across three locations, each containing three sub-locations with six items each. Narrative context was provided upon entering/leaving locations and before each sub-location in the narrative condition.
